articles.title_orig: Maker’s Mark Launches New World Wood Collection
articles.title_zh: Maker’s Mark Launches New World Wood Collection
articles.content_orig:
Maker’s Mark Launches New World Wood Collection
Maker’s Mark announced the World Wood Collection, a new Global Travel Retail-exclusive series celebrating the influence of oak from around the world.
The inaugural release, Expedition 01 , marks the first Maker’s Mark whisky to feature three oak finishes across three continents: Japanese Mizunara, French and American white oak staves.
The World Wood Collection represents the evolution of Maker’s Mark’s wood finishing philosophy, first introduced with Maker’s Mark 46, which demonstrated how oak staves could unlock new dimensions of flavor in bourbon while remaining true to the brand’s handmade heritage. Maker’s Mark has long treated oak as a key ingredient—not simply a container for its whisky, and has invested in advancing both the art of wood finishing and the stewardship of American white oak at Star Hill Farm.
“At Maker’s Mark, we celebrate bourbon as an agricultural product and the universe of flavor that can be unlocked through nature—water, wheat, oak and time,” Rob Samuels, managing director and eighth-generation whisky maker, said in a news release. “That belief has long guided our commitment to sustainable forestry and to protecting the future of American white oak. Through intentional wood finishing, The World Wood Collection explores exceptional oak from around the world to create a whisky that expands the boundaries of flavor while staying true to our craft.”
Expedition 01 brings together Japanese Mizunara, French and American white oak, with each whisky individually finished before being expertly blended into a single expression. The result is a complex, balanced whisky in which every oak contributes its own distinctive character.
“Expedition 01 represents the kind of premium, story-driven whisky experience that resonates with today’s global travelers,” Vanessa Widmann, managing director for Global Travel Retail at Suntory Global Spirits, said. “With its exclusive availability in Global Travel Retail, distinctive oak-forward story and premium presentation, it offers travelers a rare opportunity to discover a truly unique expression from Maker’s Mark — one that celebrates craftsmanship, exploration and the influence of exceptional oak.”
Available exclusively through Global Travel Retail ahead of Holiday 2026, Expedition 01 is bottled at 1L and 47.5% ABV and presented in premium packaging inspired by the distinctive grain of each oak species, reinforcing the collection’s focus on craftsmanship and discovery.
The limited-edition expression will be available beginning today in New York (JFK), London (LHR), Istanbul (SAW), Perth (PER), and Bengaluru (BLR) through Avolta retail outlets for the suggested retail price of $84.99.
For more information, visit www.makersmark.com.
Read more: Maker’s Mark to Release 2026 Cellar Aged Bourbon
In 1953, founders Margie and Bill Samuels, Sr. broke from tradition — burning the family’s 170-year-old recipe to create a bold, balanced bourbon made with soft red winter wheat for signature sweetness and creaminess. Every bottle is still hand-dipped in red wax, every barrel rotated by hand and every decision guided by the brand’s higher purpose. Maker’s Mark is proud to be both B Corp and Regenified Certified – milestones driven by the sustainability leadership at Star Hill Farm, home of the Maker’s Mark Distillery. For more information, visit www.makersmark.com .

articles.title_orig: Attorneys general cite China ties in call to end judicial training partnership
articles.title_zh: Attorneys general cite China ties in call to end judicial training partnership
articles.content_orig:
DES MOINES, Iowa  — Iowa's Attorney General is leading a group of 23 attorneys general asking the National Judicial College (NJC) to end it's relationship with an environmental organization they say has ties to China.
The NJC offers courses in courtroom skills to judges across the country. In January, the school offers a course titled "Climate Change and Water: Droughts" focusing on legal questions about water management in a changing climate. The coalition says that course was sponsored by the Environmental Law Institute (ELI).
"Judges should rule based on an impartial interpretation of the law,” said Attorney General Bird. “But if they are trained by an organization that has been influenced by another government, and a hostile one at that, that impartiality is at risk. That’s not right for Iowans who believe they are getting a fair shake when they appear in front of a judge. The NJC needs to end their relationship with an organization with ties to China.”
Earlier this month, ELI issued a statement about allegations in a report about their work. "...we have repeatedly explained our judicial education work and the principles that govern it: CJP provides voluntary, evidence-based judicial education about climate science, impacts, and solutions, and how they arise in the law. CJP does not tell judges how to rule in any case or on any issue. Nor are its programs designed to achieve a particular outcome," the statement says.
The attorneys general want the college to suspend the partnership, preserve records and review whether its educational materials were improperly influenced.
The letter does not identify a judge or court decision shown to have been influenced by China.

articles.content_orig:

The four astronauts of SpaceX’s Crew-12 mission returned to Earth this morning (Oct. 8) after nearly eight months in space.
Crew-12 's Crew Dragon capsule, named "Freedom," undocked from the International Space Station (ISS) on Wednesday morning (Oct. 7), beginning a roughly 27-hour trip back to its home planet.
Everything went well during the journey: Freedom splashed down as planned in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles today at 11:34 a.m. EDT (1534 GMT). Not long after that, the four astronauts were safely extracted from the capsule aboard a recovery ship. They'll be taken to terra firma for standard medical examinations and to begin the 45-day-long postflight conditioning process, which will help their bodies readjust to life with gravity.
"The crew is doing well. They were all smiles exiting the capsule," Bill Spetch, deputy manager of commercial, NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program, said during a post-splashdown press conference today. "It's great to have them back after 237 days in space, 235 of those on the space station."
The Crew-12 astronauts are Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway of NASA, the European Space Agency 's (ESA) Sophie Adenot, and Andrey Fedyaev of the Russian space agency Roscosmos . Meir and Fedyaev had each been to space once before, while Crew-12 was the first mission for Hathaway and Adenot.
The quartet launched to the ISS atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on Feb. 13 . Their arrival brought the station up to its normal complement of seven crewmembers. It had been operating with a skeleton crew of three since Jan. 15, when SpaceX's Crew-11 mission headed home a month early to deal with a medical issue experienced by one of its astronauts, NASA's Mike Fincke .
That was the first medical evacuation in the long history of the ISS. But it was not an emergency situation, NASA officials stressed at the time, and Fincke is doing fine now here on terra firma. (He retired in August with a total of 549 days in space, the fourth-most ever for a NASA astronaut.)
Crew-12, in turn, was relieved by the four-person Crew-13 , which arrived at the ISS last Thursday (Oct. 1). Crew-13 made it to the station less than eight hours after launch — the quickest-ever ISS trip for an American spacecraft. (The world record is just over three hours , by a Russian Soyuz crewed vehicle.)
Crew-13 was originally supposed to launch on Sept. 12. However, an issue with the propulsion system on its Crew Dragon capsule, named "Grace," pushed things back, giving Crew-12 a few extra weeks in orbit.
The Crew-12 astronauts were very busy during their nearly 10 months off Earth, performing a variety of maintenance work and dozens of scientific experiments.
Then there were the spacewalks . Meir performed four of them, bringing her lifetime total to seven. And on Aug. 18, Adenot stepped outside the ISS, becoming the first French woman ever to walk in space. She did two more over the next two weeks, including one with Meir, which was just the sixth all-female extravehicular activity in the station's history.
The Crew-12 astronauts felt a mix of emotions about their homecoming, as big transitions are always bittersweet. Indeed, Meir gave us a sense of this a few weeks back.
"What I'm looking forward to most is seeing my three-and-a-half-year-old daughter,” Meir said during a Sept. 16 call with reporters from the station.
"I'm so looking forward to seeing nature again," she added, "feeling the breeze on my face, the wind rustling through the leaves, experiencing all those things that we don't have up here. But I will very, very much miss being weightless all the time and the incredible views that we have."
Splashdown didn't wrap up all Crew-12 activities today. NASA and SpaceX will talk about the mission this afternoon, during a press conference scheduled to start at 1:15 p.m. EDT (1715 GMT). The briefing will also discuss the planned Oct. 13 launch of SpaceX's robotic CRS-35 cargo mission to the ISS. Participants are:
Editor's note: This story was updated at 8:30 a.m. ET on Oct. 7 with news of successful undocking. It was updated again at 6 p.m. ET that day to correct its headline, which previously said the Crew-12 astronauts have spent nearly 10 months in space. It was updated again at noon ET on Oct. 8 with news of successful splashdown.

The home hub is an all-new device that's like a cross between an iPad and a HomePod . It's rumored to have a 6-inch square display, and it's designed as a multi-person device to control smart home products, place FaceTime calls, watch videos, get news and weather information, stay up to date on calendar events, and more. It will integrate with Siri AI, and voice will be the main method of interaction.
Apple envisions people installing a hub in multiple rooms in the house. There will be a version meant to be mounted on the wall and a version with a half-dome speaker base, similar in design to the iMac G4. A camera and a presence sensor will detect when a person is in the room, and the device will be able to tell who it is to show a customized interface with widgets and apps. Pricing could be around $350.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: Students Rally in France for Second Day of Mass Protests in a Week
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: Students Rally in France for Second Day of Mass Protests in a Week
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of students demonstrated near Bastille Square in Paris on Thursday afternoon, as France 's nationwide student protests continue.
Crowds of students climbed the famous Bastille Monument. Some waved the French flag and sang the national anthem.
Footage from Reuters TV showed riot police charging at protesters with batons as they moved in to clear the square.
Earlier on Thursday, students barricaded Helene Boucher High School in northeastern Paris with trash bins before police broke up the protest with tear gas.
As students gathered at the school, riot police assembled in the side streets. Many protesters wore surgical masks or hoodies, apparently to avoid identification.
The school has been a flashpoint for clashes in the French capital and was one of hundreds of schools disrupted by protests on Thursday.
Although the rallies have largely been peaceful, some demonstrators have set fires and vandalized bus shelters.
In response, the police have used tear gas, batons, and blast balls. Human rights groups and children accuse officers of using excessive force.
Following an incident in which a teenager's hand was blown off, the government suspended the use of stun grenades for crowd control on Wednesday.
Since late September, when students, most of whom are under 18, began protesting to demand more education funding, police have made more than 6,600 arrests, according to the Interior Ministry.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
On Wednesday evening, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu promised that the government would present "concrete, quick, and fully funded responses" to the protests by the end of October.
Nevertheless, student protest leaders said this was not good enough and called for more marches.
In a televised address, Lecornu also lamented the "violence, students and staff being attacked, police officers and gendarmes injured, schools set on fire or vandalized, thousands of hours of classes lost, not to mention threats and insults."

articles.title_orig: Risk and strategy for Indonesia – China Marine Scientific Research cooperation
articles.title_zh: Risk and strategy for Indonesia – China Marine Scientific Research cooperation
articles.content_orig:
During the Indonesia-China foreign ministers’ meeting in Jakarta in August this year, both countries agreed to make maritime cooperation one of the main pillars of Indonesia-China strategic dialogue. One of the maritime cooperation priority agendas discussed was marine scientific research . But with China often using marine scientific research as part of its assertive maritime strategy , Indonesia should develop a plan to ensure that cooperation in this area will not threaten Indonesia’s security.
In the past few years, China has intensified marine scientific research. According to CSIS , China has more marine scientific research vessels operating in the Indo-Pacific than any other country, including the United States. Chinese research vessels operate in various locations from the South China Sea to the Indian Ocean . So how can Indonesia and China advance marine scientific research that benefits both countries while keeping national security interests in mind?
Indeed, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) encourages cooperation on marine scientific research to advance human knowledge of the ocean. Given the vastness and depth of the world’s oceans, scientists often consider them largely unexplored. But it is important to note that under UNCLOS, marine scientific research should be conducted for peaceful purposes and should not become the basis for asserting maritime claims.
For Indonesia, the world’s largest archipelagic state with a vast maritime area within its exclusive economic zone and continental shelf, knowledge of what lies beneath its waters is critical. However, with limited technology and resource capacity, international cooperation on marine scientific research is becoming very important.
But despite the benefits that Indonesia may get by conducting marine scientific research cooperation with China, it also carry significant risks. In recent years, China’s research activities have operated illegally in Indonesian waters. For instance, the research vessel Haiyang Dizhi 10 has often conducted illegal surveys in Indonesia’s Exclusive Economic Zone. Moreover, Chinese-owned uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs) have also been found operating in Indonesian archipelagic waters.
With these growing concerns, Indonesia should consider three things when developing marine scientific research that can benefit both Indonesia and China.
First, marine scientific research cooperation needs a clear definition and scope. Under UNCLOS, there are no clear definitions of marine scientific research. As a result, different parties interpret for themselves what counts as marine scientific research. A wide range of generally recognized activities include seabed topography, geology, fisheries ecosystems, marine ecosystems, genetic resources, and environmental protection.
Some other activities, despite using some of the same capabilities and data collection methods, are usually not regarded as marine scientific research. For instance, surveillance for military purposes or survey activities for oil and gas exploration are often considered not part of academic marine scientific research.
When it comes to cooperation with China, however, this scope of research can be difficult to distinguish, particularly because of the strong link between Chinese research institutions and the People’s Liberation Army. Some reports suggest that Chinese university-based research institutions supply research to the PLA . Such a close relationship may expose Indonesia’s marine data and spatial information to Chinese military institutions.
Therefore, the cooperation agreement between Indonesia and China should clearly define what activities qualify as marine scientific research and how the data may be used.
Secondly, all cooperation projects should comply with UNCLOS jurisdictional regulations. For instance, marine scientific research in the EEZ, archipelagic waters, and territorial waters should be based on the consent of coastal states. Under UNCLOS, this consent has to be specific to each research project. Indonesia therefore should maintain the requirement to secure its consent for each research activity conducted in its maritime areas under the cooperation agreement.
In the past five years alone, at least three Chinese UUVs were found in Indonesian archipelagic waters in Lombok and South Sulawesi, accidentally discovered by local Indonesian fishermen. Chinese research institutions allegedly operated these UUVs without consent and permission from the Indonesian authorities. Therefore, those UUVs operated in Indonesian waters illegally and cannot be considered legitimate.
Moreover, the type of scientific research conducted and where it is conducted can sometimes be contested. For instance, in research related to hydrography and military activities, coastal states and major maritime powers often disagree. The United States and the United Kingdom consider hydrography and military research to be allowed within the EEZ, and reject efforts by coastal states with more restrictive policies to regulate such research.
Marine scientific research can also be sensitive, particularly in a contested maritime area. For instance, even though Indonesia does not recognize any overlapping maritime claim with China, Indonesia’s EEZ overlaps with China’s illegal nine-dash line. Therefore, any research activity conducted in the overlapping area could also become very sensitive.
Thirdly, it is important to have a reciprocal agreement between Indonesian and Chinese research institutions. It should not only allow Chinese institutions to conduct research in Indonesian waters, but also allow Indonesian scholars and researchers to conduct research in Chinese waters and access information from that research.
This reciprocal agreement could not only give Indonesian research institutions more data and information, but it could also increase the possibility of technology transfer for Indonesian researchers and institutions.
Marine scientific research cooperation between Indonesia and China is important for both countries. However, given China’s aggressive maritime behavior, which often uses marine scientific research to assert its aggressive and illegal claims, Indonesia should ensure any such cooperation follows these principles so that it is not co-opted to serve China’s interests.
Cover photo: Cen Yunpeng/Xinhua/Getty Images
Aristyo Rizka Darmawan is an Assistant Professor of international law at Universitas Indonesia and a PhD Scholar at the Australian National University.

articles.title_orig: Darryl M. Bell and Kadeem Hardison Reunite for New Black Effect Podcast, “A Different World View” - iHeartMedia, Inc.
articles.title_zh: Darryl M. Bell and Kadeem Hardison Reunite for New Black Effect Podcast, “A Different World View” - iHeartMedia, Inc.
articles.content_orig:
The longtime friends and co-stars bring nearly 40 years of chemistry to the mic for an episode-by-episode rewatch, plus candid conversations on entertainment, pop culture, sports and more
Legendary “A Different World” producer and director Debbie Allen to join the series as its first guest
NEW YORK – OCTOBER 8, 2026 – iHeartMedia and Charlamagne Tha God’s Black Effect Podcast Network today announced “A Different World View with Darryl & Kadeem,” a new weekly rewatch podcast hosted by Kadeem Hardison and Darryl M. Bell. The series will premiere Thursday, October 15, with new episodes available every Thursday on the iHeartRadio app and wherever podcasts are heard.
Nearly four decades after becoming Dwayne Wayne and Ron Johnson on the groundbreaking sitcom “A Different World,” Hardison and Bell are back together and behind the mic. Each week, the pair will bring their nearly 40-year friendship and signature chemistry to conversations spanning entertainment, pop culture, sports and whatever else has their attention before heading back to Hillman. They’ll rewatch “A Different World” episode by episode, sharing behind-the-scenes stories, unpacking why the groundbreaking series continues to resonate nearly four decades later and welcoming familiar faces from the show along the way. They’ll also look ahead to the new Netflix sequel series, with conversations featuring members of both the original and new casts.
Debbie Allen will join Hardison and Bell as the podcast’s first guest, as the pair kicks off their rewatch with Season 2, Episode 2, Allen’s first episode with the series. Together, they’ll revisit how Allen came to “A Different World,” her early connection with Hardison and Bell and the transformation of the series under her leadership, while also looking ahead to the road that brought Hillman back for a new generation. Allen also serves as an executive producer on the Netflix sequel series, directs its premiere episode and appears as Dr. Langhorne.
“I am beyond excited to finally launch the ‘A Different World View with Darryl and Kadeem’ podcast,” said Bell. “Kadeem and I have only wanted to do this for over 25 years, and the time is now! I also could not be happier or think of better partners than Charlamagne Tha God, his team at The Black Effect and iHeartMedia.”
Kadeem Hardison and Darryl M. Bell are best known for their iconic roles as Dwayne Wayne and Ron Johnson Jr. on “A Different World.” Their careers have spanned film, television and production, with the pair first appearing together in Spike Lee’s “School Daze.” In recent years, they have reunited with their former castmates for the “A Different World” historically Black colleges and universities tour, celebrating the series’ lasting impact with a new generation of students. Hardison and Bell will also reprise their roles in the new sequel series.
“‘A Different World’ had an undeniable impact on Black culture, and Kadeem and Darryl are such an important part of that legacy,” said Dollie S. Bishop, President of The Black Effect Podcast Network. “We’re excited to give them a platform to bring their friendship and comedy to listeners everywhere, sharing stories fans have never heard and celebrating the series with the generations who grew up with it and those who might just be discovering it today.”
“I’ve been talking to this guy for 40 years,” said Hardison. “I’m so glad you all get to see what I’ve been dealing with. ‘A Different World View’ coming shortly!”
“A Different World View with Darryl & Kadeem” is distributed by iHeartPodcasts and is part of the Black Effect Podcast Network. Listen to the official trailer HERE . Beginning October 15, new episodes will be available every Thursday on the iHeartRadio app and wherever podcasts are heard. Video episodes will also be available on YouTube.
About Black Effect Podcast Network
The Black Effect Podcast Network is a transformative network founded by renowned cultural architect, executive producer, bestselling author and media mogul Charlamagne Tha God in a historic joint venture with the world’s No. 1 commercial podcast publisher, iHeartMedia. Charlamagne and iHeartMedia created the groundbreaking first-ever Black Effect Podcast Network, celebrating the essential Black culture-shapers on the planet—in education, entertainment, politics, pop culture, and sports. The Black Effect Podcast Network gives rise to emerging and established content creators and storytellers whose perspectives and creative visions have been marginalized and overlooked while serving an audience that has been underserved. The Black Effect Podcast Network helps its partners define their place in podcast culture through influence, ideas, and experiences that engage, inspire, inform and empower.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo's Vatican II Catechesis 27: The Mission of the Church in the Contemporary World
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo's Vatican II Catechesis 27: The Mission of the Church in the Contemporary World
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV speaks to visitors during his weekly general audience in St. Peter’s Square at the Vatican Oct. 7. Photo by CNS photo/Vatican Media
On Wednesday, Jan. 7, Pope Leo XIV announced that he would begin a new series of talks dedicated to the documents of the Second Vatican Council during his weekly general audiences. The Second Vatican Council, also known as Vatican II, was held from Oct. 11, 1962, through Dec. 8, 1965.
Pope Leo delivered the 27th installment of his catechesis, available below, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican.
Brothers and sisters, good morning and welcome!
Resuming our reflection on the Conciliar Constitution Gaudium et Spes, today we will consider the fourth chapter of the first part, dedicated to the Church’s mission in the contemporary world.
First of all, the Council recalls that the Church is not “above” or “beside” the world, but is, as it were, grafted into it. “Mundus reconciliatus Ecclesia”, wrote St. Augustine (Sermon 96): the Church is the world already reconciled with God; we are pilgrims on earth and share in this world’s fragility and beauty (cf. GS, 40).
Just as the Son of God was incarnated to give life to the world and to reconcile it with the Father, so the Church dwells in the world as a sign of the incarnation of God, in order to manifest His plan to make us all His children in one great human family. Therefore, the Church journeys through history in the midst of peoples and cultures, and “this involvement in people’s lives helps the Church understand ever more clearly that her mission has a historical scope and entails a responsibility for the way in which social relations are built” (Encyclical Letter Magnifica Humanitas , 19).
The first mission of the Church is to help people be attentive to the profound questions of life: those concerning our origin and our destiny, as well as those concerning the meaning of love and suffering (cf. GS, 41). The logic of profit at all costs and the manipulation of information risk exerting undue pressure on people to conform to a lifestyle centered on the consumption of material goods, but our hearts are made to look upwards.
The Council Fathers remind us that the Church’s mission is fulfilled also in contributing to the construction of the earthly city. However, her methods and aims are not primarily of a political order; rather, they consist in bearing witness to faith and charity, together with commitment for justice, peace, and fraternity. By worshipping Christ, the Righteous One who died for the unrighteous, the believer cannot accept the oppression of the weak and the poor, nor the unjust structures that perpetuate conditions of dependence and injustice. The social doctrine of the Church guides the actions of Christians, who collaborate with all people of good will in promoting the common good. The Church, therefore, “has no fiercer desire than that in pursuit of the welfare of all she may be able to develop herself freely under any kind of government which grants recognition to the basic rights of person and family, to the demands of the common good” (GS, 42).
To fulfil the Gospel mission effectively, it is necessary for every baptized person to commit to cooperating with the grace of the Holy Spirit, so that their faith may be living and expressed in consistent behavior. Indeed, as the Council Fathers reiterate, the discrepancy between professed faith and daily life “deserves to be counted among the more serious errors of our age” (GS, 43).
Gaudium et Spes reserves special mention (cf. ibid.) for the mission of the lay faithful who, by virtue of their Baptism, are called to enliven the world with the Christian spirit and the vision of the Gospel. The principal settings for this activity, which may well be described as priestly, are undoubtedly the family and the workplace, but it extends to every sphere of life.
Finally, the Church is always attentive to what is taking place and developing in society (cf. GS, 44). It is the task of the whole People of God, especially pastors and theologians, to discern what in the cultures of our time is worthy of consideration, always taking the Word of God and the Tradition of the Church as the supreme criteria for discernment. This requires a balanced mind, free from cultural trends, capable of viewing the world in a positive light whilst remaining steadfast in preserving and presenting the Gospel message in its entirety. Indeed, “it is certainly not by watering down the content or softening the demands that Christianity can be made attractive” (Address to the Plenary Assembly of the Dicastery for Evangelization – Section on Fundamental Questions regarding Evangelization in the World, 28 May 2026).
Dear friends, as she journeys through history, “the Church has a single intention: that God’s kingdom may come, and that the salvation of the whole human race may come to pass” (GS, 45). She strives towards this end above all through personal holiness and fraternal love. St. Paul VI wrote: “Without this mark of holiness, our word will have difficulty in touching the heart of modern man. It risks being vain and sterile” (Apostolic Exhortation Evangelii Nuntiandi, 76). Let us therefore be open to the action of the Holy Spirit, that He may help us to live in holiness and charity, so that the world may believe and hope.

articles.title_orig: Hurricane Isaias forecast to bring dangerous storm surge, with millions under warnings in US
articles.title_zh: Hurricane Isaias forecast to bring dangerous storm surge, with millions under warnings in US
articles.content_orig:
Residents in areas from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Florida urged to ‘evacuate if told to do so’
Millions of people from Louisiana to Florida are under hurricane warnings on Thursday as Hurricane Isaias looked set to head towards the US Gulf coast with weather officials warning of dangerous storm surge, hurricane-force winds, heavy rainfall, and flooding.
Isaias intensified into a hurricane from a tropical storm on Wednesday night, becoming the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.
In an advisory on Thursday morning, the National Weather Service (NWS) said that Isaias, which is currently a category 1 hurricane with sustained winds of 85mph with higher gusts, is expected to pass to the north of the Yucatán peninsula later on Thursday before reaching the northern Gulf coast where it is expected to make landfall late Friday or early Saturday.
The NWS said that Isaias is “expected to strengthen and be a strong hurricane when it approaches the northern Gulf Coast on Friday” and warned that a “life-threatening storm surge” is expected along a portion of the northern Gulf coast.
Storm surge warnings, which are issued when there is a “danger of life-threatening indundation from rising water moving inland from the coastline”, are in effect on Thursday from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Steinhatchee, Florida , and residents in the warning area have been urged to “follow advice given by local officials and evacuate if told to do so”.
Hurricane warnings, meaning that hurricane conditions are expected, are also in effect in the areas from Ocean Springs, Mississippi to the Bay/Gulf county line, Florida. The NWS has warned that “damaging hurricane force-winds are expected over portions of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama, and southern Mississippi” and urged residents to prepare for the possibility of “long-duration power outages”.
The NWS warned on Thursday: “Gusty winds are possible in portions of the Yucatan Peninsula today.”
Isaias is also expected to bring “areas of heavy rainfall” to the central Gulf coast and much of the south-east from Friday into the weekend, and the NWS said that flash and urban flooding, along with isolated river flooding, will be possible. From Friday through the weekend, Isaias is expected to produce rainfall amounts of three to seven inches across the central US Gulf coast extending from far south-eastern Louisiana to the Florida Big Bend region.
“Localized totals up to 15 inches are possible, particularly within banding across the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend,” the NWS said.
Isolated tornadoes are also possible on Friday night in coastal areas of Alabama and the Florida Panhandle and far southwestern Georgia, the NWS said, adding that “the tornado threat will continue Saturday for eastern Alabama, Georgia and northern Florida.”
On Wednesday, the Alabama governor, Kay Ivey, declared a state of emergency in 40 counties, saying that the order “will allow us to take any needed steps ahead of landfall”. The emergency declaration is scheduled to remain in effect until 14 October.
The Florida governor, Ron DeSantis, also declared a state of emergency this week for 25 counties as the state prepares.
“This order ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida,” DeSantis said in the announcement.
At the local level, officials in Okaloosa county, Florida, declared a local state of emergency on Wednesday and ordered some residents in coastal areas to evacuate. Panama City also declared a local state of emergency “due to the potential effects of Isaias and its near threat to the citizens and property in Panama City and surrounding communities”.
Several school districts in Alabama and Florida have also announced closures ahead of Isaias.
The Federal Aviation Administration also warned on Thursday that Isaias may “lead to Gulf route closures”.
In Tennessee, the NWS office in Morristown warned that “remnants of Hurricane Isaias will bring heavy rain and strong, gusty winds to our area this weekend.” The office said that “high winds could top 60–70+ mph in the eastern TN mountains and foothills, with isolated flash flooding possible in heavy rainfall areas.”

articles.title_orig: Health officials report 74 new measles cases in Pennsylvania - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Health officials report 74 new measles cases in Pennsylvania - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
Five people have died in the state so far this year.
Pennsylvania is reporting 74 new measles cases since Monday, the state's health department said Wednesday.
A total of 1,078 cases have been reported in the state so far this year. At least 207 people have been hospitalized and five people have died, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) .
"Of the 74 cases added, more than 40 represent individuals who were sick more than two weeks ago and are no longer contagious, but their cases were only recently reported and subsequently confirmed, the DOH said. Wednesday's update "does not reflect a current surge in new infections."
Of the five people who died, two of the deaths were among unvaccinated adults: an 18-year-old and a 40-year-old. The other two deaths were among infants who were too young to have received the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine.
The fifth death occurred in an unvaccinated resident of Lancaster County, in southeastern Pennsylvania, but it is unclear how old the individual is. Lancaster County is the epicenter of the state's outbreak, with 401 cases confirmed so far.
One-third of cases are among those under 18 years old and fewer than 1% of cases are among those fully vaccinated with the MMR shot, according to DOH data.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. One dose is 93% effective in preventing measles infection and two doses are 97% effective, the CDC says.
Infants aged 6 to 11 months living in or traveling to high-risk outbreak areas may receive an early third dose of the MMR vaccine.
CDC data, however shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025-26 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019-20 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.
"State health center staff have administered more than 5,700 MMR vaccinations at 198 pop-up vaccination clinics in the affected communities since the outbreak began in late April," DOH wrote in a press release on Wednesday.
"Dozens of additional vaccine clinics are scheduled for the upcoming weeks and months, based on community interest and need," the press release continued. "In pop-up clinics and at state health centers combined, Department nurses have administered nearly 9,000 MMR vaccine doses to residents across the Commonwealth in 2026."

articles.title_orig: Cyborg Politics 3.0: AI and the Algorithms of Unpeace
articles.title_zh: Cyborg Politics 3.0: AI and the Algorithms of Unpeace
articles.content_orig:
https://doi.org/10.60965/bq31-tt86
Today’s debate about the perils and promises of artificial superintelligence is at once terrifyingly existential and astonishingly narrow. It is framed as a good vs. evil binary over humanity’s future: superabundant Utopia or humanity’s extinction. No-one can put a number on the probability of any outcome because the titans of Silicon Valley are accelerating into the unknown.
In this essay, author Alex de Waal argues that this framing misses what has already happened. AI has changed how we think, as members of a social-political collective. AI has hacked the operating system of society and is defining the questions to be posed and limiting the range of allowable answers to those questions.

articles.title_orig: Trump says he is considering asking FBI to investigate the death of Nolan Wells
articles.title_zh: Trump says he is considering asking FBI to investigate the death of Nolan Wells
articles.content_orig:
Lawyers for Wells’s family have called for a federal investigation into 18-year-old’s disappearance and death
On Wednesday, Donald Trump said he was considering asking the FBI to investigate the death of Nolan Wells, a Black college freshman who was last seen alive on a 4 July boating trip with friends.
Wells, 18, went missing while on Horn Island, a barrier island off the coast of Mississippi . His body was found on the island two days later. Wells’s cause and manner of death are still undetermined.
His disappearance and subsequent death have become a flashpoint for racial animosity in the country, drawing national scrutiny. During the Jackson county investigation into the case, social media became rife with misinformation about Wells, his family and his friends.
Wells’s mother, Christine Wells-Wonsley, started searching for him, leading to a photo of Wells with three white friends on a boat going viral.
In the months between Wells’s body being found and a Jackson county grand jury declining to indict anyone in his case, many have suggested that the treatment Wells’s family has received by local officials would have been different if they were white.
Wells’s family and Ben Crump, the civil rights lawyer who is representing the family, have called for a federal investigation into Wells’s disappearance and death, after a Jackson county grand jury’s decision to decline to indict anyone in the case.
The Jackson county grand jury determined that Wells drowned. However, an independent autopsy conducted by the president of the Howard University hospital, Roger A Mitchell Jr, a forensic pathologist, determined there was no evidence of drowning due to the absence of water in Wells’s stomach, lungs and throat. That autopsy also noted bruising on Well’s head, back, left shoulder and buttocks.
“We do not believe Nolan drowned, and the blunt force trauma to his head cannot be ignored or explained away,” Crump said in a statement. “Nolan’s family deserves the truth, and we will keep fighting until every question is answered and justice is served.”
On Tuesday, Crump and Wells’s parents joined Cynthia Choi, Stop AAPI Hate’s executive director, in calling for a federal investigation into Wells’s death and disappearance. The California congresswoman Maxine Waters, the Florida congresswoman Frederica Wilson and others also sent a letter to Jessica Bowron, the acting director of the US National Park Service (NPS), noting that most of Horn Island is federally designated land and calling on the NPS’s investigative services branch to open a “prompt and exhaustive investigation” into Wells’s disappearance and death.
“Today, I am asking the people whose job it is to serve and protect to keep their word to our family,” Elmore Wonsley, Wells’s father, said at the press conference. “Our son was found on federal land, and we are asking the FBI to step in and do a full investigation. We’re not asking for special treatment. We’re asking for what any father would do for his child, and that’s to find the truth about what happened to his child.”
As he was leaving the White House, reporters asked Trump whether he planned to push the FBI to launch an independent investigation into Wells’s death.
“Well, we’re looking at that,” he said. “Yes, we are.”
“Sunday will mark 100 days since we have been looking into the death of Nolan Wells, so when President Trump responds to news reporters that ‘we’re looking into it’, we believe that carries more weight than the response given by the FBI,” Crump said in a statement. “Our team stands ready to work with the federal government to ensure Nolan’s death is investigated to the fullest extent.”

articles.title_orig: Vance suspends Microsoft, others from foreign workers applying for green cards, alleges visa 'abuse'
articles.title_zh: Vance suspends Microsoft, others from foreign workers applying for green cards, alleges visa 'abuse'
articles.content_orig:
Check out what's clicking on FoxBusiness.com.
Vice President JD Vance and Labor Department officials announced Thursday that the Trump administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and others from a key employment-based green-card program, accusing major tech firms and outsourcing companies of abusing the visa system at the expense of American workers.
"There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," Vance said at a news conference on H-1B and J-1 visa fraud, noting the administration was targeting companies that he accused of using foreign workers to undercut U.S. wages and replace American employees.
Vance said Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers last year while benefiting from 6,300 H-1B visas and nearly 3,000 green cards, calling it a "scandalous system."
"For every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with 1½ foreign indentured servants," Vance said.
MICROSOFT UNVEILS CODE OF CONDUCT FOR AI MODELS AS SAFETY CONCERNS MOUNT
Texas Congresswoman Beth Van Dyne discusses the Trump administration's proposed $100,000 fee on H-1B visa filings. She highlights systemic abuses within the program, including active fraud investigations in North Texas.
Vance said the administration had decided to suspend Microsoft’s access to the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program, which allows employers to sponsor foreign workers for permanent residency .
"Our message to Microsoft is, you're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers," Vance said. "You cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants."
The Department of Labor was also suspending Adobe from the program, along with several major IT outsourcing firms – Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini among them – according to Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, citing active federal investigations.
"We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," he said. "Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They've received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications.
"That's hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers. Our historic action is the first critical step to stop the fraud and the abuse, and ensure that these programs never come at the expense of the American worker," he said. "Under President Trump's leadership and thanks to Vice President Vance and this task force, we are ending the fraud that has fueled reliance on foreign labor."
Vice President JD Vance and Labor Department officials announced Thursday that the Trump administration is suspending Microsoft and others from a key employment-based, green-card program, accusing the tech giant of abusing the U.S. visa system. (Cesc Maymo / Getty Images)
FOX Business reached out to Microsoft and Adobe for comment.
Vance also announced investigations into alleged J-1 visa abuse at several universities, including Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown, the University of Pittsburgh, UC Davis, Caltech, Arizona State and MIT. "I am announcing a historic investigation into the J-1 visa fraud involving nine major American universities," Labor Department Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said. "Subpoenas have been served, investigations are underway, and nobody will be getting a free pass because their name is carved into an expensive building."
"Improperly using J-1 visa classifications to avoid employment obligations, exploit taxpayer-funded programs and undermine American workers will not be tolerated," he added.
US ECONOMY ADDED 29,000 JOBS IN SEPTEMBER, A SLOWER PACE THAN EXPECTED
Vance denounced what he called the "insult" of visa fraud by America's companies.
"This is a fundamental insult to the American worker and to the American way of life," Vance said. "We cannot allow visa programs that were designed to ensure that American corporations had access to the best and the brightest, to use them to undercut the wages of American workers."
Vance urged Congress to reform the program for its loopholes to abuse.
The Trump administration is considering ending H-4 spouse work permits for H-1B visa holders. Former acting ICE director Jonathan Fahey discusses the economic impact on American workers.
"This is a terribly pernicious system: It's gone on for too long, and we'd all encourage, by the way, Congress to do something about it," Vance said.
"I, again, would encourage Congress to reform this program. It is very clear that it's not working the way that it should, but we have tools in the administration to make this program work better for the American people. A lot more we could do if Congress was willing to play ball," he continued. "And again, we extend an invitation to both Democrats and Republicans. If you want the H-1B visa program to stop being used to defraud the American taxpayer and to undercut the wages of American workers, get to work, and we will help you, but we're going to do everything that we can in the interim to ensure the program works as it was designed for."
GET FOX BUSINESS ON THE GO BY CLICKING HERE
When asked about targeting companies, Vance was detailed in saying it was intended to change companies' behavior and not punish them. But Attorney General Todd Blanche did warn there could be criminal cases brought against companies or individuals, too, that have been found to have broken U.S. law.
"Microsoft is a great American company, and we have a great relationship with them," Vance responded to the first question. "They do a lot of important things. They also laid off 6,000 American workers, while replacing them with 6,300 H-1B. And our message to Microsoft is not that we want to harm your company, it's that we want your company to thrive, but we want it to thrive by employing and empowering your fellow Americans."

Aims to Provide One Million Meals to Children in Need
NEW YORK, NY / ACCESS Newswire / October 8, 2026 / TABLE FOR TWO USA (TFT) invites everyone to participate in the 12th Annual ONIGIRI ACTION that will run from Thursday, October 8 to Tuesday, November 17, 2026 to provide one million school meals to children in need. During the campaign, through the generosity of our partner organizations (see below), every rice ball related post to the campaign website or social media with #OnigiriAction will provide five school meals to children in need. TFT will enhance school meals in socioeconomically disadvantaged neighborhoods in the U.S. by adding fresh vegetables and fruits to school lunches. TFT will additionally provide school meals to children in East Africa.
Our ONIGIRI ACTION campaign commemorates United Nations' World Food Day. As a nonprofit organization with roots in Japan, the campaign highlights onigiri (rice balls), which are a traditional Japanese comfort food made with love to share with others.
Since its launch in 2015, ONIGIRI ACTION has supported over twelve million school meals. TABLE FOR TWO has additionally received two prestigious awards: one related to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) and the other for health and culture from the Japanese government ( https://bit.ly/3Kg0ZHY ). Amid rising food prices driven by climate change, geopolitical instability, and ongoing global economic uncertainty, concerns are growing that Zero Hunger, one of the Sustainable Development Goals, will not be achieved. As these pressures continue to mount, the need for TFT to deliver healthy meals to those in need becomes more critical every year.
TFT and our partners will host numerous virtual and in-person events to celebrate ONIGIRI ACTION. Through onigiri, we can have meaningful connections and shared cultural experiences. Together with Japanese consulates across the United States, we are organizing the Onigiri Diplomacy Project. Consulates will post photos with #OnigiriAction, display the campaign poster and props, and in some cases organize an interactive onigiri experience or event. We will additionally run Intercollege Onigiri Action, a fun and collaborative initiative on Instagram for college students in the U.S. The group with the most onigiri posts will win, and special awards will also be given for the most creative reel and best group photo. There will also be special Nationwide Shared Table hybrid cooking event supported by Japan Foundation New York where participants nationwide will learn how to make creative and delicious onigiri.
Event information and updates will be announced on our website and social media .
Partner Organizations in the U.S.: For every onigiri photo posted, five school meals will be provided through the generous support of our partners: J.C.C. Fund/Japanese Chamber of Commerce and Industry of New York, JFC International/Nishiki, JCAW, Zojirushi America, San-J, ITOCHU International & ITOCHU Europe, SMBC Americas Foundation, Misuzu Corporation, MUFG Bank, Mishima Foods U.S.A., Kewpie Americas, and Six Tree Foundation. Onigiri partners: BentOn, Onigilly, Sunny Blue, Omusubee
To Learn More: ONIGIRI ACTION (USA site): https://usa.tablefor2.org/onigiri-action ONIGIRI ACTION (Global site): https://onigiri-action.com/en/
Products with Donations: During the campaign, a portion of the proceeds from products below will be donated to provide school meals: Nishiki rice (JFC International), rice cookers (Zojirushi America), tamari soy sauce (San-J), Tamaki Gold (ITOCHU International), inari (Misuzu Corporation), nori komi furikake (Mishima Foods U.S.A.), KEWPIE mayonnaise (Kewpie Americas), okonomiyaki pancake mix (Otafuku Foods).
About TABLE FOR TWO USA: TFT is a 501(c)(3) organization that addresses hunger and health issues caused by unhealthy eating by educating people about healthy eating habits and providing nutritious school meals to those in need. TABLE FOR TWO started in Japan and now operates globally. As one of the most well-known NPOs in Japan, a country celebrated for the longevity of its people, TFT USA promotes Japanese healthy eating culture and has launched innovative programs, ONIGIRI ACTION, Wa-Sho - Learn. Cook. Eat Japanese! - and Edamame Champ, featuring Japanese food culture to tackle critical health issues.

articles.title_orig: Thousands to march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen
articles.title_zh: Thousands to march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen
articles.content_orig:
Rally to remember woman, 87, whose rent battle with investment firm triggered nationwide protests over housing crisis
Thousands of people are expected to march through the centre of Madrid on Thursday evening in memory of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her flat in the capital a fortnight before her death triggered mass protests over Spain’s housing crisis .
The pensioner, whose flat had been bought by an investment firm that sought to increase her rent by 230%, had become the public face of the crisis before her death in hospital on Wednesday night.
Abascal’s eviction unleashed waves of demonstrations across Spain, led to the setting up of a protest camp in the centre of the capital, and prompted the socialist-led government to propose emergency measures to try to make the rental market more equitable. When those measures were voted down by rightwing and far-right parties last week, the prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, announced a snap general election , to be held on 29 November.
Anger over the plight of the woman who had become known around the country as Maricarmen remained undimmed a few hours after her death. On the pavement across from the apartment building where she had lived for seven decades, a steady stream of people visited a small, steadily growing memorial. Some came to light candles or leave flowers, while others left handwritten messages such as, “You made history Maricarmen,” and “Thank you for changing Spain”. Sara, 41, who had come with her young son and a sign that read, “Maricarmen, we’ll fight for you”, said: “We’re here because I think Maricarmen’s death shows how institutions can kill a person by failing to care for them.”
For many, the site was a reminder of all that Maricarmen had gone through as she tried to stay in her home, fending off three eviction attempts before the investment firm succeeded in forcing her out. “When people are protected less than investors, that leads to these kinds of things happening,” Sara added. “This woman could have died – if she had died of natural causes – she could have died peacefully in her home.”
Jaime, 34, pointed to all that Maricarmen had come to represent, particularly in a country like Spain, where social rights are supposedly guaranteed. “She had become a symbol, albeit one she never wanted to be, of the fight for decent housing,” he said. “So I came here because I think it’s important to restore some of the respect that Spanish society took away from Maricarmen.”
Visitors included some of the housing campaigners who had helped Maricarmen fight off previous eviction attempts. “This is really hard to take,” said Miguel, 59, fighting back tears as he added a red rose to the memorial. “When money is more powerful than people’s lives, it’s unbelievable.”
He said he hoped Maricarmen’s death would mark a turning point in Spain. “At least now we’re talking about this and putting names to those who are being evicted,” he said. “Because until now, there were 44 people a day being forced out of their homes. To the people in power, those are just numbers – now at least we’ve started putting names to those going through this.”
The Madrid tenants’ union announced a commemorative march at 8pm on Wednesday from the camp in the Puerta del Sol square to Abascal’s flat.
“Farewell, Maricarmen!” the union said in a post on social media . “Tonight we’ll honour you with a march … to the place that was your home for 70 years, and where you just wanted to stay until the end.”
Abascal’s ordeal has made housing a key issue in the forthcoming election, with Sánchez’s government seeking to push a redrafted package of measures through the council that operates when parliament has been dissolved. Meanwhile, the rightwing and far-right parties that opposed the legislation in congress last week have accused the prime minister of failing to act to address the housing crisis over the course of his eight years in office.
Sánchez offered his condolences to Abascal’s family and friends on Wednesday night. “A hug also to everyone who’s feeling this loss today as their own,” he wrote on social media. “Rest in peace.”
after newsletter promotion
Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the leader of the conservative People’s party (PP), which voted against last week’s emergency measures, also offered his condolences.
“No campaigning, no political parties, no partisan ends, no more bricks in the wall,” he wrote on social media. “When a person dies, there should be nothing but respect.”
The following day, however, Feijóo accused the government of trying to “manipulate the emotions of the Spanish people” by focusing on one particular eviction when there had been countless others during Sánchez’s time in office.
PP politicians also joined forces with the far right on Thursday to veto attempts to hold a minute’s silence for Maricarmen in Madrid’s regional parliament and the country’s senate. In Madrid’s municipal council, meanwhile, a rightwing attempt to block a minute’s silence was thwarted by opposition parties.
Abascal’s death has prompted reflection on how she had been treated by politicians and the media. The far-right Vox party, which also voted down the new decrees, had falsely suggested that Maricarmen would have had a home had she been an immigrant from North Africa , while one commentator had opined that “Maricarmen was chosen during a casting call for people facing eviction” to become a leftwing saint.
At least two far-right figures, including one of Vox’s MEPs, sought to sow doubt over the cause of Abascal’s death, with one even suggesting an autopsy should be carried out to determine whether the government had been involved . Another wrote : “Maricarmen was probably already made to send in her postal vote before they did her in. I expect anything from this scum.”

articles.title_orig: Harvard celebrates World Mental Health Week
articles.title_zh: Harvard celebrates World Mental Health Week
articles.content_orig:
From October 13-16, 2026 Harvard will host World Mental Health Week , a series of events and activities focused on supporting student mental health and wellbeing. Throughout the week, students can participate in guided meditation sessions, pet therapy sessions, and craft activities such as flower bouquet making and watercolor painting.
The events will take place following World Mental Health Day on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Each year, World Mental Health Day inspires organizations around the world to share resources and plan events in the pursuit of destigmatizing mental health challenges and encouraging the transformation of mental health services. This year’s theme, “ Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change, ” highlights the power of lived experiences in transforming how we approach mental health challenges, develop strategies to address them, and deliver services to those in need.
Schools and departments across the University are collaborating with the Office of the Associate Provost for Student Affairs to sponsor events, including workshops and discussion sessions.
Highlights include a fireside chat sponsored by Harvard Medical School Center for Bioethics, the Harvard Medical School Department of Global Health and Social Medicine, and Countway Library, in which Dr. Vikram Patel, Paul Farmer Professor and chair of Global Health and Social Medicine at Harvard Medical School and Dr. S. Abbas Shobeiri, Division Chief of Benign Gynecology and Director of the Pelvic Floor Program at Inova Health System, will explore trauma and healing and how storytelling and art can help approach mental health differently.
Another highlight includes a seminar at the Lee Kum Sheung Center for Health and Happiness at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health with Dr. Lauren Taylor, assistant professor of Population Health at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine, which will explore the role of trust in healthcare delivery.
Find a listing of all activities, as well as strategies, tools, and resources for maintaining or improving mental health at: https://www.harvard.edu/wellbeing/.
In addition to the services available from Harvard’s Counseling and Mental Health Services (CAMHS) and the Center for Wellness and Health Promotion (CWHP), students can access mental health providers and services through TimelyCare, a virtual health and wellbeing platform, designed to expand access to no-cost mental health and wellness services for registered students.

articles.title_orig: The Story Behind the Butterfly’s Enhanced Visual World of Color
articles.title_zh: The Story Behind the Butterfly’s Enhanced Visual World of Color
articles.content_orig:
Researchers discovered the genetic switch that produces extra light-detecting cells that led to the ability to recognize more colors in flowers and other butterflies
Many insects see the world through hundreds of tiny lenses that are grouped together in a visual organ known as the compound eye. Behind each lens sits a cluster of eight light-detecting cells arranged in a pattern that scientists believe has existed for hundreds of millions of years.
Butterflies are the rare exception. They are equipped with nine light-detecting cells, which gives them the ability to visually navigate a much richer world of color, compared with insects such as flies, and allows them to locate nectar and potential mates.
University of California San Diego scientists in School of Biological Sciences Associate Professor Michael Perry’s lab have discovered the genetic modification that gave butterflies this visual advantage.
“Butterflies see far more color than flies do because at some point in their evolution they added a photoreceptor to every unit of their compound eye — a rare break from an eye design that has otherwise been conserved across insects for hundreds of millions of years,” said Perry, a faculty member in the Department of Cell and Developmental Biology. “We found the genetic switch that did it.”
In a study published in the journal Science Advances , Perry and his coauthors identified the genetic steps involved in the emergence of the ninth photoreceptor in painted lady butterflies, the most widespread butterfly species in the world. While flies feature light-sensing cells known as photoreceptors R1-R8, butterflies expanded their color vision by adding a second R7 photoreceptor to each unit of the eye, the researchers found. To test whether that genetic change was enough on its own, they recreated it in a fruit fly — switching on a gene in cells that normally keeps it off, and timing it to the brief window when the eye is being built. This produced a “butterfly fly” that grows its eyes on the butterfly plan, with nine cells per eye unit instead of eight.
Antibody stains in a developing butterfly retina show that each unit eye contains two R7 color photoreceptors. Credit: Perry Lab, UC San Diego
A new light detector in the eye would be of no use if the brain is not able to connect to the new information provided by that detector. The scientists assumed that adding a sensory input such as a new photoreceptor unit should require the brain to slowly evolve a matching neuron partner that would receive information on the other end. That didn’t happen, the researchers found. To their surprise, no adaptive change was needed.
The fly brain regularly overproduces neurons that die off if they fail to find a connection. The brain of the butterfly-fly, they found, knew precisely how to handle the new photoreceptor by using its extra “standby” neurons and put them in play.
“When we gave those spare neurons something to connect to, they survived and wired up correctly — immediately — with no further genetic change,” said Perry. “In other words, the brain was ready before the eye asked. This is a rare, concrete case of evolution making use of neurons that were otherwise going to die.”
The new study’s findings provide a glimpse of how insects, with a flexible brain framework, were able to accommodate new inputs to evolutionarily adapt to an emerging need in their environment: an elevated ability to visualize flowering plants.
The team also found a hawkmoth that appears to be partway through the same transition: the lower half of its eye is butterfly-like, with two of these cells per unit, while the upper half is fly-like, with one. That is roughly what you would expect if the change began in one region of the eye and spread.
The research team is now exploring further unanswered questions, such as the difficult-to-study issue of whether the butterfly-fly can in fact see more vivid color with the additional photoreceptor, as butterflies do.
The research team included Ke Gao, Julia Ainsworth, Antoine Donati, Yunchong Zhao, Michelle Franc Ragsac, Cara Genduso, Zoie Andre, Andrew Tomlinson and Michael W. Perry. The researchers acknowledge support from: the National Institutes of Health (1T32GM133351); a Hellman Fellowship (Hellman Fellows Fund); a National Science Foundation CAREER award (2339031); and an NIH National Human Genome Research Institute grant (R01HG013634) from the EDGE program.

articles.title_orig: 'Tired' Catherine Zeta-Jones delivers unexpected reaction to Michael Douglas' bombshell memoir
articles.title_zh: 'Tired' Catherine Zeta-Jones delivers unexpected reaction to Michael Douglas' bombshell memoir
articles.content_orig:
Catherine Zeta-Jones recently shared what she really thinks of her husband Michael Douglas ' new memoir titled One Helluva Ride, which was released on October 6.
The actress visited Today on October 8, where she got candid about the book.
Willie Geist inquired: "I've gotta ask you, because I was just telling you, I interviewed your husband Michael Douglas yesterday. He's got a memoir out. He told me, and I'm curious if this is true, that you have not read the book yet?"
Michael and Catherine have been married since 2000 (@ Instagram)
Catherine admitted: "It's true." She explained: "Look, I've just finished [shooting] Wednesday [for] season three. We shot in Dublin for seven months, and then I just literally got on a Ryanair plane and landed in London – did all of the Kill Jackie stuff."
The movie star continued: "Then I went to Bilbao, Spain, and now I'm here talking to you Willie on the fabulous Today show."
Aside from sharing her packed itinerary, she joked: "And as much as I love my husband, when I'm tired at night, I have no intention of reading about him…at all."
Regardless of the fact that she didn't read the book yet, she advertised: "But everyone else should. The book is called One Helluva Ride, and I think everyone should hold onto their cowboy hats, because I think it is."
Being that that memoir goes into depth about not only Michael's successful career, but his marriage with the actress, Willie teased what Michael told him in his recent Today interview.
Catherine opened up about her husband's memoir (@ Getty Images)
Willie recalled: "He told me that he came home the other night, sort of peeked around the corner, and you didn't seem upset, so he thought, 'Okay, we're in good shape.'"
Catherine charmingly replied: "He caught me in a good time," as she laughed.
The couple, who have been married since 2000, know a thing or two about longevity, and it's apparent that humor is a huge part of their personal secrets to success.
Catherine admitted that she hasn't read the memoir (@ Getty Images)
Michael shared his insight with People on what makes a marriage work long-term, confirming: "A good sense of humor doesn't hurt, number one."
He continued: "And talking things out. Never using the words 'never' or 'always' when you get angry with each other. And putting yourself in the other person's position before you make your value judgment."
Catherine added that she has "no intention" to (@ Instagram)
Overall it comes down to enjoying each other's company and sharing hobbies together as a form of bonding.
Michael continued: "But you gotta have fun. When I first met her, I said, 'Do you like golf?' She said, 'I love golf.' Well, I melted."

articles.title_orig: Google Cloud introduces Gemini agent for work as AI race heats up
articles.title_zh: Google Cloud introduces Gemini agent for work as AI race heats up
articles.content_orig:
Google on Thursday unveiled a new AI agent tailored for workplace tasks, positioning it to compete with other technology giants racing to offer their own virtual office assistants.
Called Gemini, the AI is a "universal agent" that can write and run code, create images and media and integrate with Google products like Gmail, Docs, Drive and Sheets, as well as third-party apps like Slack and Microsoft 365, Google said in its statement .
Thomas Kurian, the CEO of Google Cloud, shared the new product during a keynote address at Gemini at Work 2026 on Thursday, an annual event where Google showcases its suite of AI technology.
Google said the agent can seamlessly integrate into people's workflow, acting like a co-worker that can carry out tasks autonomously. Workers can delegate tasks to the agent, and it will return a finished product, Kurian said in the company's blog post.
"Gemini can function as your personal assistant or as a team member, where it works on behalf of a group of people, like a project manager within a team, or on behalf of a specific role in an organization, like an analyst in your finance department," he wrote.
To execute on certain tasks, Gemini can create its own "sub-agents," which Google described as "temporary, job-specific agents, each with their own identity," that can work together to accomplish goals over several days.
The AI agent, which runs in the Cloud, is designed to build memory and skills based on the tasks it's assigned and the questions users ask it.
"You never have to re-brief it or wonder which machine you told it to do something on," Kurian wrote in the blog post.
Gemini joins a growing field of AI agents marketed for personal and workplace use. In September, Meta introduced Muse , a personal AI assistant that has been downloaded millions of times. OpenAI followed suit late last month with the introduction of "Dots" , an "AI helper" available to ChatGPT users with Pro and Business Premium accounts.

articles.title_orig: ‘I just want to hold him’: USS Lincoln sailor to meet his 10-month-old son as ship docks
articles.title_zh: ‘I just want to hold him’: USS Lincoln sailor to meet his 10-month-old son as ship docks
articles.content_orig:
After more than 300 days at sea, the USS Abraham Lincoln is finally come back home to San Diego. NBC 7’s Dana Williams reports.
Among the thousands of family members awaiting to greet their loved ones as they step off the USS Abraham Lincoln will be 10-month-old Nathan, who is meeting his father for the first time.
Brent Ledbetter is an air traffic control center officer aboard the aircraft carrier. His son was born in November, about a week after Ledbetter reported to the ship, NBC News reported.
Stream San Diego News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC 7.
"I just want to hold him, play with him,” Ledbetter told NBC News. “He’s crawling around now, so I’m excited to chase him around the house and give him all the love that, that, you know — have been kind of withheld for the last 10 months. I’m so excited."
Ledbetter told NBC News his wife is also an air traffic control officer and had been assigned to the Lincoln. He replaced her on the ship shortly before she gave birth.
Among the roughly 5,000 sailors and Marines onboard the Lincoln, there are more than 50 babies waiting for a parent’s return on Thursday when the ship docks at Naval Air Station North Island.
What began as a Pacific deployment with a spring return soon shifted to a prolonged stay at sea as the carrier was diverted to Middle East to support the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran. Over the next several months, the crew would endure deployment extensions, supply shortages and deteriorating mental health.
Now, after nearly a year at sea, the beleaguered Lincoln is almost home and crewmembers who are parents will be among the first allowed off the ship.

articles.title_orig: USS Abraham Lincoln to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.title_zh: USS Abraham Lincoln to dock in San Diego after harrowing stretch at sea
articles.content_orig:
Deployment for nearly a year was marked by reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among crew
The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been deployed for nearly a year and has spent months supporting US military operations against Iran, is scheduled to dock in San Diego on Thursday afternoon.
It marks the end of a deployment that has been described as “one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era” and that became marked by a record-setting stretch at sea, repeated deployment extensions, and reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among some crew members.
The Lincoln left San Diego last November, initially bound for the Pacific. But it was redirected to the Middle East after the US and Israel launched their war with Iran in late February. The carrier remained there until late August, when it was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its journey home .
Earlier in August, the Lincoln’s deployment made headlines and faced scrutiny as reports began surfacing about poor living conditions onboard the ship, including shortages of supplies and water, plumbing problems, low morale and worsening mental health among the roughly 5,000 personnel on the carrier. Two leading military newspapers also reported that there had been two attempts by sailors to jump overboard, causing concern among families and military health experts.
The reports prompted outrage from Democrats , while senior officials in the Trump administration pushed back . Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, called the reports “completely misrepresented ”, and when reporters asked Donald Trump if he thought the deployment had gone on too long, he responded : “Not nearly long enough” – a comment that angered some naval families.
In a statement at the time, Adm Brad Cooper, who heads US Central Command, claimed that of the US navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, the Lincoln had “among the lowest number of cases related to mental health”. But he said that “this doesn’t mean that all is perfect”.
Cooper said that a long deployment at sea “is uniquely challenging and tough, and every single one of us, including me, reacts to stressors in different ways”.
Two weeks ago, as the Lincoln headed back to San Diego, Hung Cao, the acting navy secretary, acknowledged that eight service members from the Lincoln and its accompanying strike group attempted to take their own lives.
Sara Jacobs, a Democrat representing California’s 51st district who visited the Lincoln in late September, said in a statement last week that while she is “relieved that the USS Abraham Lincoln will soon be back in San Diego” and “looking forward to welcoming them home”, her “demand for accountability won’t end when they make port”.
“I will continue pushing for an [office of the inspector general] investigation into these conditions and a House armed services committee field hearing in San Diego to hear directly from these service members,” she said. “We need to prevent this crisis from happening ever again, and ultimately end the Iran war and bring all our service members home.”
On Wednesday, Hegseth visited the Lincoln ahead of its return, and praised the crew. He acknowledged that their deployment had not been “easy”.
“When you greet your families tomorrow, just pass my gratitude from the president and myself,” Hegseth said. “Let them know that their long wait, we believe, was in service of a righteous and historic mission.”
During his remarks, Hegseth announced that those onboard the vessel would be awarded the presidential unit citation, which, according to the US military , is conferred on units of the armed forces “for extraordinary heroism in action against an armed enemy”.
Ahead of the Lincoln’s arrival on Thursday afternoon, Blue Star Families, one of the largest US-based non-profit organizations supporting active military service members, veterans and their families, said in a statement that “every homecoming is an important moment for military families”.
The organization said that it “welcomes home the sailors of USS Abraham Lincoln and wants every family to know they’re not alone as they reconnect”.
In the weeks ahead, Blue Star Families said it will host appreciation days for Lincoln sailors and their families, including several events next month in San Diego.
